item.arguments: Use $fw:debug on issue #182. It describes a production bug in the retry flow.
special_constraints: Start from the issue report when possible.
success_definition: Begins from issue intake.
Moves into evidence and root-cause work.
Does not jump straight to code edits.

item.arguments: Use $fw:debug on this stack trace: nil pointer in webhook retry handler after timeout.
special_constraints: Require a failing test or reproducer before the fix.
success_definition: Explains the causal-chain expectation.
Calls for a red failing signal.
Keeps debugging ahead of fixing.

item.arguments: Use $fw:debug on this bug where the code follows the current design, but the design now conflicts with real user needs.
special_constraints: Route upstream when the design is the problem.
success_definition: Recognizes this can become a design, architecture, or requirements issue.
Routes to the right upstream stage rather than papering over it.
Still preserves the reproducer as the truth surface.

item.arguments: Use $fw:debug on a live production degradation where rollback vs patch is still unclear and the only current evidence is alerts, logs, and traces.
special_constraints: Debug should not flatten active incident framing into ordinary bug fixing.
success_definition: Recognizes when incident handling should come before local debugging.
Routes to $fw:incident while preserving the evidence-first posture.
Does not jump directly to a fix plan before the incident frame is set.

item.arguments: Use $fw:debug on a flaky checkout failure that only happens around 1% of the time in CI and has no obvious stack trace.
special_constraints: Require a stronger reproduction loop before hypothesizing a fix.
success_definition: Treats reproduction-rate improvement as the first debugging goal.
Proposes looping, stress, seeding, timing, or isolation tactics to raise the failure rate.
Does not claim a fix path before a usable feedback loop exists.

item.arguments: Use $fw:debug on an endpoint that became 4x slower after the latest release, with no functional failures.
special_constraints: Distinguish performance regression diagnosis from generic optimization.
success_definition: Creates or asks for a baseline measurement before fixes.
Uses profiling, query plans, bisection, or differential comparison as evidence.
Keeps the path focused on causal regression proof rather than speculative tuning.

item.arguments: Use $fw:debug on a user report that says "customers sometimes see wrong totals" but provides no environment, logs, fixture, or reproduction steps.
special_constraints: Do not invent a cause when the feedback loop cannot be built yet.
success_definition: Identifies the missing reproduction or artifact as the blocker.
Lists concrete loop-building attempts or artifact requests such as logs, traces, fixtures, HAR files, or environment access.
Stops short of prescribing a fix without a credible feedback loop.
